title: Phayao Kingdom
capsule: The Kingdom of Phayao was a Tai polity in what is now northern Thailand, founded from the older principality of Ngoenyang and centred on Wiang Phayao in the upper Ing River basin. Its greatest ruler, Phaya Ngammueang (r. 1261–c. 1330s), presided over the kingdom's apex and was a principal member of the celebrated Three Kings alliance forged with Mangrai of Lanna and Ramkhamhaeng of Sukhothai, a pact that shaped the political landscape of mainland Southeast Asia. The kingdom extended across parts of modern Chiang Rai, Phayao, Lampang, Phrae, and Nan provinces. In 1338 the forces of Khamfu of Chiang Saen and Phaya Phanong of Nan jointly sacked Phayao, forcing the last ruler Khamlue to flee, after which Khamfu annexed the territory into Lanna.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's core territory is moderately well attested through Thai chronicles, but precise boundaries and earlier ruler reigns depend on sources compiled centuries after the fact, so territorial mapping carries significant uncertainty.
